citations.quote: Assume AC and the hypotheses and notation of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]]. Let $R_n=R_{L_n,N_n}$ be the finite phase reference of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], let $A_n$ be the constructed band, and set $M_n^{\rm ph}(E)=R_n(E\cap A_n)/R_n(A_n)$. Let $C_n^{\rm ph}$ be the full fixed-$N_n$ canonical probability. Then $D_n=D(M_n^{\rm ph}\Vert C_n^{\rm ph})$ satisfies $D_n/V_n\to0$. This is a mathematical statement about a normalized measure restriction; it does not assert $D_n\to0$ or global total-variation convergence.

Assume AC. Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$, use the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|_2$ from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], define $|x|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$, and use the numerical coordinate conventions in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. A finite configuration is a finite subset $\omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with no repeated points; its number of points is $N(\omega)$. A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$. Define
$$H_\phi(\omega)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y),\qquad H_\phi(\varnothing)=0.$$
The sum is over unordered two-point subsets, so every term is evaluated at a nonzero separation; if any term is $+\infty$, the sum is $+\infty$.

The potential is stable if some $B\geq0$ satisfies $H_\phi(\omega)\geq-BN(\omega)$ for every finite configuration. It is superstable in the Georgii splitting convention if $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$, where $\phi_s$ is stable and $\phi_r\geq0$ everywhere and, for some $r_0,\delta>0$, $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta$ whenever $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$. It is lower regular if a nonnegative nonincreasing $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfies
$$\phi(x)\geq-\psi(|x|_\infty),\qquad \int_0^\infty\psi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr<\infty.$$
It is regular if it is lower regular and, for some $R<\infty$, $\phi(x)\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ whenever $|x|_\infty\geq R$. These are the conventions used for the interacting results on this page. A genuine divergent positive core is the separate additional condition that some nonincreasing $\chi:(0,r_1]\to(0,\infty)$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_1$ and $\int_0^{r_1}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=+\infty$; it is not implied by superstability.

For $L>0$ put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $V_L=L^d$, and let $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ be $H_\phi$ for configurations restricted to $\Lambda_L$. For a regular potential and sufficiently large periodic cubes, periodize $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ by $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and set
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x}\phi(y-x),$$
interpreting the value as $+\infty$ if a positive infinite term occurs. Under this regularity hypothesis, the far image sum is absolutely convergent for all sufficiently large $L$ by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]; this is the image convention used below. With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where the tuple notation means $H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N):=H_\phi(\{q_1,\ldots,q_N\})$ when the coordinates are distinct, and $H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N):=+\infty$ on collision diagonals. The integrand is therefore zero on collisions; these diagonals have product Lebesgue measure zero by the no-collision construction in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], so this convention leaves all partition integrals unchanged. For $N=0$ the empty tuple has energy zero. Here $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$. The normalized unit-intensity Poisson version is $Z_Q(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,\mathrm{free}}}]$; since the Poisson density contributes $e^{-V_L}$, $\Xi(L;z,\beta)=e^{V_L}Z_Q(L;z,\beta)$. A physical pressure identification is not part of this mathematical definition.

For a probability law $P$ on the configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], stationarity means $P\circ T_x^{-1}=P$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^d$. When $P$ is stationary and $E_PN_{[0,1)^d}<\infty$ (finite intensity), write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$. Use the finite-region relative entropy $D$ defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. If $\phi$ is stable with constant $B$, then $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}\geq-BN_{\Lambda_L}$, so the negative part of $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ is $P$-integrable for every such $P$. Whenever the limit exists, write
$$\mathcal E(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}E_PH_{L,\mathrm{free}},\qquad I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
In the variational results below, $\Phi(P)$ denotes this same positional energy density: $\Phi(P):=\mathcal E(P)$. The cited results establish existence under their stated hypotheses; this definition does not assume either limit exists for every stationary finite-intensity law.

Let $\phi=\phi_s+\phi_r$ be superstable in the splitting convention of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Suppose $H_{\phi_s}(\omega)\geq-B_sN(\omega)$ and $\phi_r(x)\geq\delta>0$ for $|x|_\infty\leq r_0$, with $\phi_r\geq0$ elsewhere. For the unit cells $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$, there are constants $A>0$ and $B\geq0$ such that every finite configuration satisfies
$$H_\phi(\omega)\geq A\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}N_{C_i}(\omega)^2-BN(\omega).$$
Only finitely many summands are nonzero. This is the cell form used in the continuum pressure arguments.

Let $d\geq1$ and let $\phi$ be a regular potential with a nonnegative nonincreasing envelope $\psi:[R_0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, where $R_0<\infty$ and $\int_{R_0}^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)dr<\infty$. Thus $|\phi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ for $|x|_\infty\geq R_0$. For $g>2R_0$ set
$$\eta(g)=g^d\psi(g)+\int_g^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)dr.$$
Then $\eta(g)\to0$ and
$$\sum_{m=1}^\infty m^{d-1}\psi(mg)\leq 2^{d-1}g^{-d}\eta(g).$$
Moreover, there is a choice $g(\ell)>0$, for all sufficiently large real $\ell$, such that $g(\ell)\to\infty$, $g(\ell)/\ell\to0$, and
$$\left(\frac{\ell}{g(\ell)}\right)^d\eta(g(\ell))\longrightarrow0.$$
For every fixed finite configuration and all sufficiently large periods $L$, the noncoincident periodic-image tail $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d,\ |k|_\infty\geq K_0}|\phi(x-y+Lk)|$ is absolutely convergent. The tail of the cell envelope $\psi(|j|_\infty-1)$ over all sufficiently large integer offsets is summable. This lemma is a deterministic tail estimate; it uses no superstability or thermodynamic-limit conclusion.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB, and the superstable regular interaction of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], $\beta>0$, and an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. For integers $N_L$ with $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, let $Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)$ be the $1/N_L!$-normalized positional partition on the periodized cube, with the image convention of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Then
$$L^{-d}\log Z_{\mathrm{per}}(L,N_L;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the same rate as the free cube. Let $C^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,N_L}$ be the periodic exact-$N_L$ canonical law and $R_{L,\omega}$ its periodized empirical field from [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]]. For any finite supporting activity $z>0$ of $F_\beta$ at $\rho$, these empirical fields concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of the minimizer set of $I+\beta\Phi-\rho\log z$. Writing $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$ for this minimizer set, the concentration means $(C^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,N_L})^*\{\omega:R_{L,\omega}\notin U\}\to0$ for every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of it. Here outer probability is as defined in [[lem-tdmath-canonical-empirical-field-conditioning]], and equals ordinary probability for measurable events. A singleton minimizer gives convergence in probability in this outer-probability sense in $\tau_L$.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let
$$\mathcal H_c:=\{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega): I(P)\leq c\},\qquad c\in[0,\infty),$$
where $I$ and the local-tame topology $\tau_L$ are defined by [[thm-tdmath-specific-entropy-density]] and [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]. Then $\mathcal H_c$ is compact and sequentially compact in $\tau_L$. This is a pure measure-theoretic compactness theorem for simple locally finite configurations relative to the independent unit-intensity Poisson reference; it makes no thermodynamic-limit or physical claim.

Assume AC and let $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}(\Omega)$, with this class defined in [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], be stationary for the translations of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. For a bounded Borel set $G$, write $P_G$ and $Q_G$ for the restrictions of $P$ and the unit-intensity Poisson reference $Q$ to configurations in $G$. For $L>0$, put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and
$$D_L:=D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
Then the specific relative entropy density
$$I(P):=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{D_L}{L^d}$$
exists in $[0,+\infty]$ and satisfies
$$I(P)=\sup_{m\in\mathbb N,\ m\geq1}\frac{D(P_{\Lambda_m}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_m})}{m^d}.$$
If $I(P)<\infty$, every bounded Borel restriction has finite relative entropy. This is an information functional relative to the specified unit-intensity Poisson law; changing the reference changes its value.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and fix $z,\beta>0$. Use the stationary finite-intensity law space $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$, the specific relative entropy $I(P)$, the intensity $\rho(P)$, and the positional energy density $\Phi(P)=\mathcal E(P)$ defined in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] and [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]]. The existence and lower semicontinuity of $\Phi$ under these hypotheses are established below. For free and periodic cubes define
$$Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}\!\left[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,bc}}\right],\qquad bc\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}.$$
Then the limit $p_Q(z,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z_{L,z,\beta,bc}$ exists, is independent of $bc$, and
$$p_Q(z,\beta)=-\min_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in the local-tame topology $\tau_L$. This theorem concerns positional configurations only. If $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}$ is instead normalized against Lebesgue measure with $1/N!$, then $\Xi_{L,z,\beta}=e^{L^d}Z_{L,z,\beta,\mathrm{free}}$, so its logarithmic rate is $p_Q+1$.

Let $F_\beta$ be the finite concave canonical rate on the interior attainable-density interval from [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Extend it by $F_\beta(0)=0$, by its interior upper-semicontinuous limit at any finite upper endpoint of its effective domain, and by $-\infty$ outside the closed effective domain; retain the value $-\infty$ if the endpoint limit is $-\infty$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta),$$
whose existence is [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\bigl(F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\bigr),\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\bigl(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\bigr)$$
for every $\rho$ in the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$. These are thermodynamic limits of positional partition functions. They do not assert local-observable equivalence, a finite-volume endpoint realization, or a thin energy-shell limit.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB. Use the model and dimensionless energy $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]. Let $L_n\to\infty$, $V_n=L_n^d$, and integers $N_n$ satisfy $N_n/V_n\to\rho>0$, where $\rho$ is an interior attainable density for the positional canonical rate. Fix $b>0$. Assume $F_b(\rho)$ is the periodic exact-particle log-partition rate supplied by [[thm-tdmath-periodic-fixed-n-limit]] for every $b'$ in a neighborhood of $b$, and is differentiable at $b$. Write $C_n^{\rm ph}$ for the full fixed-$N_n$ canonical law, and define
$$e_b(\rho)=-\partial_bF_b(\rho)+\frac{d\rho}{2b}.$$
Then, for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, there exist $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $n_0$ such that
$$C_n^{\rm ph}\!\left(\left|\mathcal H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e_b(\rho)\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le 2e^{-c_\varepsilon V_n}\quad(n\ge n_0).$$
Consequently there is a nonincreasing sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$ for which the full phase band
$$A_n=\{N=N_n,\ |\mathcal H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e_b(\rho)|\le\delta_n\}$$
has $C_n^{\rm ph}(A_n)\to1$. It has positive finite phase-reference measure for all sufficiently large $n$. This constructs a controlled shrinking window; it makes no claim about every prescribed shell width or an exact energy surface.

Assume AC. Fix $d\geq1$ and let $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be the numerical even Borel pair potential. Assume the stability, cell-superstability, lower-regularity, and decreasing-integrable-tail conditions of [[def-csm-stable-superstable-continuum-interaction]], with its fixed cell side $\ell$, and the superstable regular interaction, unit-coordinate, and periodic-image conventions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. These are model hypotheses; the definitions do not prove that a particular material satisfies them. Use the finite-region phase-space and statistical-state conventions of [[def-csm-statistical-state-observable]].

Let $E_0>0$ joules be the energy unit, $\ell_0>0$ metres the length unit, $m>0$ kilograms the particle mass, and $p_*>0$ kg m s$^{-1}$ the momentum reference. A physical position vector $\mathbf q_{\rm phys}\in\mathbb R^d$ in metres has dimensionless numerical coordinate $x=\mathbf q_{\rm phys}/\ell_0$. From here on, $q\subseteq\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ denotes a finite configuration of these numerical coordinates, so the physical cube has side $\ell_0L$ and its points are $\ell_0x$. Each momentum mark $p_x\in\mathbb R^d$ is an SI momentum vector in kg m s$^{-1}$. Write $V_L=L^d$ for numerical volume. Fix also a primitive positive scalar conversion parameter $k_B$ with units J K$^{-1}$, called the Boltzmann constant: the thermal-energy scale assigned to temperature $T$ is $k_BT$ joules. Its value is fixed as part of the model data, not derived by this mathematical definition. If $T>0$ kelvin, put $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and $b=\beta_{\rm phys}E_0=E_0/(k_BT)>0$.

The potential $\phi$ in the two interaction suppliers is numerical in units of $E_0$ and takes dimensionless displacements as input. For a physical displacement $\mathbf r\in\mathbb R^d$ measured in metres, its pair-potential map is $V_{\rm pair}(\mathbf r):=E_0\phi(\mathbf r/\ell_0)$ joules. For a finite positional configuration $q\subseteq\Lambda_L$, set $U_{L,\mathrm{free}}(q):=H_\phi(q)$ using [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and set $U_{L,\mathrm{per}}(q):=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(q)$ using that item's periodic-image sum. The periodic definition is used only for periods for which that sum is defined; the large-$L$ results below use sufficiently large periods as supplied there. Thus $E_0U_{L,bc}$ is the dimensional pair energy in either boundary convention.

Let $Q_L$ be the unit-intensity Poisson probability on positional configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, defined by [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Its $N$-particle conditional law $Q_{L,N}$ is uniform on the unordered simple $N$-point configurations; in labelled coordinates it is $L^{-dN}dx_1\cdots dx_N$ on the no-collision set. A finite marked configuration in this sector is a simple set $\xi=\{(x,p_x):x\in q\}$ with $q\subseteq\Lambda_L$, $N(q)=N$, and $p_x\in\mathbb R^d$. Equip the finite marked sector with the sigma-algebra generated by the counts $N_{A\times C}(\xi)=\#\{(x,p_x)\in\xi:x\in A,\ p_x\in C\}$ for bounded Borel $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and Borel $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$. Let $\lambda_d$ be Lebesgue measure on the SI numerical momentum coordinates and set $r:=p_*^{-d}\lambda_d$. For each fixed $q=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}$, define $r^{\otimes q}$ as the image of $r^{\otimes N}$ under $(p_1,\ldots,p_N)\mapsto\{(x_j,p_j):1\le j\le N\}$; this is independent of the enumeration of $q$ because $r^{\otimes N}$ is permutation-invariant. The cell-code representation in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]] supplies a measurable enumeration on each finite sector, so $q\mapsto r^{\otimes q}$ is a measurable kernel for the marked-count sigma-algebra. The finite phase reference is
$$R_{L,N}(dq,dp):=Q_L(dq)\,r^{\otimes q}(dp)\,1_{\{N(q)=N\}}.$$
It is sigma-finite, meaning the marked sector is covered by countably many measurable sets of finite reference measure: for each integer $k\geq1$, restrict to marks satisfying $|p_x|\leq kp_*$ for every one of the $N$ points. These sets exhaust the sector, and their reference measures are at most $Q_L(N(q)=N)r(B_k)^N<\infty$, where $B_k=\{p:|p|\leq kp_*\}$ satisfies $r(B_k)\leq(2k)^d$ because it lies in the box $[-kp_*,kp_*]^d$ of Lebesgue volume $(2kp_*)^d$ by the box-volume supplier in the dependency closure of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. The factor $e^{-V_L}/N!$ from the Poisson sector is retained. In physical coordinates the corresponding one-particle product scale is $h_{\rm ref}^d=\ell_0^dp_*^d$, an action to the power $d$; it is a reference convention, not a derived quantum constant.

For a marked configuration define the total dimensionless energy
$$\mathcal H_{L,bc}(q,p)=U_{L,bc}(q)+\sum_{x\in q}K(p_x),\qquad K(p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2mE_0}.$$
The corresponding physical Hamiltonian is $H^{\rm phys}_{L,bc}:=E_0\mathcal H_{L,bc}$ joules, so $\beta_{\rm phys}H^{\rm phys}_{L,bc}=b\mathcal H_{L,bc}$.
For $b>0$, [[lem-csm-gaussian-mark-moments]] gives $\kappa_b=\int e^{-bK}r(dp)=(2\pi mE_0/(bp_*^2))^{d/2}$ and the probability kernel $\nu_b(dp)=\kappa_b^{-1}e^{-bK(p)}r(dp)$. Whenever the positional canonical partition is finite and positive, nonnegative product integration [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] gives exact identities
$$Z^{\rm ph}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b)=\int e^{-b\mathcal H_{L,bc}}dR_{L,N}=\kappa_b^N Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b),\qquad C^{\rm ph}_{L,N,bc}=C^{\rm pos}_{L,N,bc}\,\nu_b^{\otimes q}.$$
Here $Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}=E_{Q_L}[1_{\{N(q)=N\}}e^{-bU_{L,bc}}]$ and the canonical probabilities are the normalized respective integrands. Under a full grand preparation of activity $z_{\rm ph}$, integrating each momentum changes the positional activity to $z=z_{\rm ph}\kappa_b$; thus a positional activity $z=e^\alpha$ corresponds to $z_{\rm ph}=e^\alpha/\kappa_b$. These are exact definitions and normalizations; they do not assert dynamical equilibration or finite-volume grand convergence. Write $\mathbb T_L^d:=\mathbb R^d/L\mathbb Z^d$ for the periodic position space, represented by $\Lambda_L$; translations act modulo $L$, and the translation-average is Lebesgue measure on $\Lambda_L$ divided by $V_L$. For periodic boundary conditions, simultaneous translation of all positions modulo the period preserves $R_{L,N}$ and $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$: the conditional position law is uniform on $\mathbb T_L^d$, the mark reference is invariant under relabelling points, and the image energy depends only on pair displacements. Hence normalized canonical and finite band restrictions are invariant under every such translation.

Assume AC. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on one measurable space and use $D(P\Vert Q)$ as defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q)=\sup_{\phi\in B_b}\left(P(\phi)-\log Q(e^\phi)\right),$$
where $B_b$ is the set of bounded real measurable functions. In particular $D\geq0$. If $T$ is measurable, then $D(P\circ T^{-1}\Vert Q\circ T^{-1})\leq D(P\Vert Q)$.

For standard-Borel spaces $X,Y$, probability reference measures $Q_X,Q_Y$, and a joint probability $P_{XY}\ll Q_X\otimes Q_Y$ with finite $D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)$, let $P_{Y|X=x}$ be the conditional law supplied by [[thm-conditional-density-formula]]. Then
$$D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)=D(P_X\Vert Q_X)+\int_X D(P_{Y|X=x}\Vert Q_Y)\,P_X(dx).$$
More generally, for random variables $R,S,Y$ taking values in standard-Borel spaces $\mathcal R,\mathcal S,\mathcal Y$, with $R=r(S)$ for a measurable $r:\mathcal S\to\mathcal R$, and a probability reference $Q_Y$ on $\mathcal Y$, the conditional increments
$$G(R):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|R}\Vert Q_Y)\right],\qquad G(S):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|S}\Vert Q_Y)\right]$$
satisfy $0\leq G(R)\leq G(S)$ whenever $D(P_{S,Y}\Vert P_S\otimes Q_Y)<\infty$.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the cube $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and the translation $T_x$ defined in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. For a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, let $\omega^{(L)}=\{q+Lk:q\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ be its periodic continuation. Define its **periodized empirical field**
$$R_{L,\omega}:=\frac1{L^d}\int_{\Lambda_L}\delta_{T_x\omega^{(L)}}\,dx.$$
The integral is the push-forward of normalized Lebesgue measure on $\Lambda_L$ under $x\mapsto T_x\omega^{(L)}$. For any probability law $C_L$ on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L$, define its **empirical-field barycenter** as the probability mixture
$$\bar C_L(B)=\int C_L(d\omega)R_{L,\omega}(B)$$
for every measurable configuration event $B$. By [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], for a nonnegative measurable test $f$, the mixture identity holds with values in $[0,+\infty]$. For a signed local tame $f$ from [[def-tdmath-local-tame-topology]], the finite expectation formula
$$\bar C_L(f)=\int C_L(d\omega)R_{L,\omega}(f)=\frac1{L^d}\int_{\Lambda_L}E_{C_L}[f(T_x\omega^{(L)})]\,dx$$
is asserted when $\int C_L(d\omega)R_{L,\omega}(|f|)<\infty$. In particular $E_{C_L}N<\infty$ suffices: if a bounded support $A$ is contained in a box of side $a$, then $N_A(T_x\omega^{(L)})\leq (\lceil a/L\rceil+2)^dN(\omega)$ uniformly in $x$. The growth bound $|f|\leq b(1+N_A)$ therefore gives absolute integrability. For stationary laws write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}\in[0,+\infty]$, with finite intensity meaning $\rho(P)<\infty$; this agrees with the finite-intensity convention in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. This is a spatial average over the finite box, not the raw finite-volume law viewed at a fixed origin.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). For $L>0$ and a finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ with $N(\omega)=N$, the measure $R_{L,\omega}$ of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]] is a stationary probability law of finite intensity and
$$\rho(R_{L,\omega})=\frac{N}{L^d}.$$
For any probability law $C_L$ on finite configurations in $\Lambda_L$ with $E_{C_L}N<\infty$, its empirical-field barycenter $\bar C_L$ is also a stationary probability law of finite intensity and $\rho(\bar C_L)=E_{C_L}N/L^d$.

Assume AC, fix $d\geq1$ and $\lambda>0$, and let $Q_\lambda$ be the configuration law of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Define the intensity measure on Borel sets by $\Lambda_{Q_\lambda}(A):=E_{Q_\lambda}N_A$, where $N_A=\omega(A)$ and the nonnegative expectation may be infinite. For pairwise disjoint bounded Borel sets $A_1,\ldots,A_r\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, the restrictions $\omega|_{A_1},\ldots,\omega|_{A_r}$ are independent, each count $N_{A_j}$ has Poisson law with mean $\lambda|A_j|$, and the joint law of counts on any finite disjoint family is the product of those Poisson laws. In particular, $Q_\lambda$ is invariant under every translation $T_x$, and $\Lambda_{Q_\lambda}(A)=\lambda|A|$ for every Borel $A$. For every bounded Borel $A$ and real $a$, its count also has the exact exponential moment
$$E_{Q_\lambda}e^{aN_A}=\exp\!\left(\lambda|A|(e^a-1)\right).$$
Every finite product of standard Borel spaces, with its finite product sigma-algebra, is standard Borel.

Assume AC. If $B$ is a Borel subset of a Polish space $(P,\tau)$, then $B$ has a finer Polish topology with exactly the trace sigma-algebra $\mathcal B(P)|_B$. In fact there is a finer Polish topology on $P$ with the same Borel sets which makes $B$ clopen. Thus $(B,\mathcal B(P)|_B)$ is standard Borel.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For any set $I$, standard-Borel coordinate spaces $(E_i,\mathcal E_i)$, and consistent finite-dimensional laws $(\mu_F)_{F\Subset I}$, there is a unique probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal C_I$ whose $F$-coordinate marginal is $\mu_F$ for each finite $F$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces. Then:

1. the set function $E \mapsto (\mu \times \nu)(E)$ of
   [[def-product-measure-on-sigma-finite-spaces]] is a measure on
   $\mathcal A \otimes \mathcal B$;
2. for measurable rectangles,
   $$(\mu \times \nu)(A \times B)=\mu(A)\nu(B),$$
   with the nonnegative extended-product convention $0\cdot\infty=\infty\cdot0=0$;
3. the measure $\mu \times \nu$ is sigma-finite; and
4. it is the unique measure on $\mathcal A \otimes \mathcal B$ with the
   rectangle formula.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$. For $i\in\mathbb Z^d$, let $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$. These are left-closed, right-open cells. For every $x\in\mathbb R^d$, [[lem-integer-part]] supplies the unique integers $i_j$ with $i_j\le x_j<i_j+1$, so $x$ belongs to exactly one $C_i$. The cells are Borel products of closed/open ray intersections and have volume one by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], whose statement covers this face convention. A finite configuration in $C_i$ is a finite subset of distinct points. Encode it by its cardinality $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and its uniquely lexicographically increasing list of local coordinates $(x_1-i,\ldots,x_n-i)\in([0,1)^d)^n$. Pad the code after its first $n$ coordinates with the zero vector. For fixed $n$, the strictly increasing lists form a Borel subset of $([0,1]^d)^n$, since lexicographic strict order is a finite union of coordinate-equality and coordinate-inequality conditions. Thus all codes form a Borel subset of $\mathbb N_0\times([0,1]^d)^{\mathbb N}$. Each factor $[0,1]^d$ is Polish as a closed subspace of complete $\mathbb R^d$ with a countable dense rational grid; $\mathbb N_0$ with its discrete metric is Polish. The ambient space is Polish by [[cor-countable-products-and-g-delta-subspaces-of-polish-spaces-are-polish]] (and is completely metrized by [[lem-standard-complete-metric-on-a-countable-product]]), so [[lem-borel-subspaces-admit-polish-presentations]] makes the cell space $E_i$ standard Borel. By [[lem-tdmath-counts-generate-configuration-sigma]], its sigma-algebra is generated by the counts $N_B$ for Borel $B\subseteq C_i$.

derivations.claim:
1.1 Put D_n=D(M_n^ph || C_n^ph), and let B_n be the positional marginal. The conditional chain rule gives
$$D_n=D(B_n||C_n^pos)+E_{B_n}D(b_n(.|q)||ν_b^{⊗N_n}),$$
so D(B_n||C_n^pos)≤D_n by the conditional chain rule [F8]. The canonical positional density relative to full Poisson probability Q_Λn is 1_{N=N_n} exp(-bU_n,per)/Z_Q,n^pos, where Z_Q,n^pos=exp(-V_n)Z_n,N_n^pos. Integrating the log likelihood against B_n gives
$$D(B_n||Q_{\Lambda_n})+bE_{B_n}U_{n,per}=D(B_n||C_n^{pos})-\log Z_{Q,n}^{pos}\le D_n-\log Z_{Q,n}^{pos}.$$
By [F1] and [F4], V_n^-1 log Z_Q,n^pos→F_b(ρ)-1; hence the right side divided by V_n has limsup at most 1-F_b(ρ). [A1, F1, F4, F8, algebra]

2.1 For every sufficiently large $n$, the periodized-image series is absolutely convergent by [F3]. Given a finite $q\subset\Lambda_{L_n}$ in the shell, form $q_M=\bigcup_{a\in\{0,\ldots,M-1\}^d}(q+L_na)$. Since $L_n$ is an integer, its unit-cell occupation pattern repeats exactly $M^d$ times. In the pair sum for $H_\phi(q_M)/M^d$, each fixed image offset $k\in\mathbb Z^d$ has multiplicity factor $\prod_{j=1}^d(1-|k_j|/M)_+$, which tends to $1$ and is bounded by $1$. For finite periodic energy, absolute convergence lets us first restrict to finitely many offsets with arbitrarily small omitted absolute tail; the factors converge on that finite set and keep the omitted tail bounded, so $H_\phi(q_M)/M^d\to U_{n,\mathrm{per}}(q)$. If any image term is $+\infty$, the desired lower bound is automatic. Applying [F2] to $q_M$, dividing by $M^d$, and taking the limit proves $U_{n,\mathrm{per}}\geq A\sum_iN_{C_i}^2-BN_n$; the same replication applied to the stability bound proves $U_{n,\mathrm{per}}\geq-B_0N_n$. On the full shell from [F7], $U_{n,\mathrm{per}}=\mathcal H_n-\sum K\leq V_n(e_b+\delta_n)$. The periodized cell bound yields $E_{B_n}\sum_iN_{C_i}^2/V_n\leq A^{-1}(e_b+\delta_n+B N_n/V_n)$, uniformly bounded. Because $L_n$ is an integer, its torus is tiled by $V_n$ unit cells; torus translation invariance makes all $E_{B_n}N_{C_i}^2$ equal, so each is bounded by the preceding sum divided by $V_n$. Cauchy–Schwarz then gives a uniform bound $E_{B_n}N_{C_i}N_{C_j}\leq C$ for every pair of cells. For the negative pair terms, each bounded-distance cell has finitely many neighboring cells and each term is bounded below by $-2B_0$ by [F2]; for remaining offsets, [F3] supplies the summable envelope $\Psi$. Hence the expected sum of negative pair magnitudes is $O(V_n)$, and so is the total negative part of $U_{n,\mathrm{per}}$. The shell upper bound on $E U_{n,\mathrm{per}}$ then gives $E_{B_n}U_{n,\mathrm{per}}^+=O(V_n)$. Since the sum of positive pair terms equals $U_{n,\mathrm{per}}$ plus the sum of negative pair magnitudes, its expectation is also $O(V_n)$. Therefore $E_{B_n}|U_{n,\mathrm{per}}|=O(V_n)$. [F1, F2, F3, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Let $\widetilde g_n=\widetilde g(L_n)$ be the real corridor width supplied by [F3] at $L_n$, and set $g_n=\lceil\widetilde g_n\rceil$. Then $g_n\to\infty$ and $g_n/L_n\to0$, and $a_n=L_n+g_n$ is an integer. By [F11], take independent tile configurations with law $B_n$ on $\mathbb Z^d$ and independently choose a uniform phase in $[0,a_n)^d$. The map from these data to the union configuration is measurable: for each bounded Borel observation set, only finitely many tile indices can meet it, and each resulting count is a finite sum of Borel indicators of the finite cell-coordinate lists. Thus the constructed law $P_n$ is well-defined and locally finite. Translating the phase preserves its uniform law and only relabels the independent, identically distributed tiles, so $P_n$ is translation-stationary. Put $\rho_n=N_n/V_n$. Its intensity is $N_n/a_n^d=\rho_nV_n/a_n^d\to\rho$. For a fixed local-tame test $f$ supported in a bounded set $A$, choose $r$ larger than its coordinate diameter. The random phase puts $A$ wholly inside an occupied tile with probability at least $(L_n-2r)^d/a_n^d\to1$. On this event torus translation invariance of $B_n$ gives exactly its local law. For any Borel set $E\subseteq\Lambda_{L_n}$, torus invariance and the exact count $N_n$ give
$$E_{B_n}N_E=\frac1{V_n}\int_{\mathbb T_{L_n}^d}E_{B_n}N_{E+y}\,dy=\frac{N_n|E|}{V_n}.$$
The first equality uses invariance; for each fixed configuration, the integral in the numerator sums over its $N_n$ points, and each point lies in $E+y$ for a set of translations of measure $|E|$. Apply this identity to each occupied portion of $A$ on the bad phase set; gap portions contain no points. The phase-averaged expectation of $(1+N_A)$ on that set is at most its probability times $1+\rho_n|A|$. Since $|f|\leq C(1+N_A)$ and $\rho_n$ is bounded, $P_n(f)-B_n(f)\to0$. [F1, F2, F3, F7, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Fix $n$ and a lattice phase, and restrict to a large observation cube. Its intersections with complete occupied tiles have independent laws $B_n$; its gap pieces are empty; and only $O_n(\text{surface area})$ tile intersections meet the observation boundary. The Poisson restrictions on these disjoint pieces are independent by [F10]. For each complete occupied tile, the relative entropy is $D(B_n\Vert Q_{\Lambda_{L_n}})$; restriction contraction [F8] bounds each boundary-tile contribution by this same finite value. An empty gap piece $G$ has entropy $D(\delta_{\varnothing}\Vert Q_G)=-\log Q_G(\varnothing)=|G|$. Product additivity follows by iterating the chain rule [F8]. For the mixture over the uniform phase, integrate the variational objective from [F8] for any bounded test and bound it by the phase-average conditional entropy; taking the supremum shows the mixture entropy is at most that average. Divide by observation volume and let the cube grow: the complete-tile density tends to $a_n^{-d}$, the gap-volume density to $(a_n^d-L_n^d)/a_n^d$, and the boundary contribution to zero. The specific-entropy limit exists by [F5], so
$$I(P_n)\leq\frac{D(B_n\Vert Q_{\Lambda_{L_n}})+a_n^d-L_n^d}{a_n^d}.$$
For the energy comparison, assign half of each pair term to each endpoint cell. Step 2.1 gives $E_{B_n}N_{C_i}N_{C_j}\leq C$ uniformly, a bound $O(V_n)$ on the total negative pair magnitude, and a bound $O(V_n)$ on the total positive pair sum: the latter is the total energy plus the negative pair magnitude, hence is bounded by the positive part of the total energy plus that magnitude. Fix $R>R_0$. Periodic-image pairs of torus separation at most $R$ that are absent from the finite-tile free energy $U_{L_n,\mathrm{free}}$ cross a tile face; their endpoints lie in a boundary strip of width $R+1$ containing $O(RL_n^{d-1})$ unit cells. The negative contribution per such cell is bounded by the finite number of near offsets, $\phi\geq-2B_0$ from [F2], and the pair-count bound; the expected positive contribution per cell is bounded by the total positive pair-sum estimate and torus translation invariance. Thus the expected absolute fixed-range discrepancy divided by $V_n$ is $O(R/L_n)$. For remaining pairs, [F3] bounds the expected absolute energy per volume by $C\sum_{|k|_\infty>R-c_d}\Psi(k)$, tending to zero as $R\to\infty$. Cross-tile pairs have separation at least $g_n$; the same tail bound with cutoff $g_n$ tends to zero as $g_n\to\infty$. Taking first $n\to\infty$ at fixed $R$ and then $R\to\infty$ therefore gives $\Phi(P_n)=E_{B_n}U_{n,\mathrm{per}}/a_n^d+o(1)$. Combining the entropy bound, step 1.1, and $a_n^d/V_n\to1$ gives
$$\limsup_n[I(P_n)+b\Phi(P_n)]\leq1-F_b(\rho).$$
Here the gap fraction vanishes because $g_n/L_n\to0$. [F1, F2, F3, F5, F8, F10, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Stability gives $\Phi(P_n)\geq-B_0\rho(P_n)$, so step 4.1 bounds $I(P_n)$. Compactness [F5] supplies a convergent subsequence from every subsequence. If $P$ is a cluster point, intensity is continuous in $\tau_L$ because the unit-cell count is a local-tame test, hence $\rho(P)=\rho$. Lower semicontinuity and step 4.1 give $I(P)+b\Phi(P)\leq1-F_b(\rho)$. Subtract $\alpha\rho$ and apply the variational lower bound and exact minimum [F6]; $P$ must attain the grand variational minimum. The singleton hypothesis forces $P=P_*$. Thus every cluster point is $P_*$, compactness gives $P_n\to P_*$, and step 3.1 gives $B_n[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every local-tame $f$. By [F9], $\bar B_n$ is stationary with intensity $N_n/V_n$, and torus invariance gives $\bar B_n(f)=B_n[f]$; therefore $\bar B_n\to P_*$ in $\tau_L$. For the exact-$N_n$ canonical law $C_n^{\rm pos}$, [F4] says its periodized empirical field $R_{L_n,\omega}$ converges in outer probability in $\tau_L$ to $P_*$. For a local-tame $f$ with $|f|\leq c(1+N_A)$, [F9] makes $X_n:=R_{L_n,\omega}(f)$ measurable and gives $|X_n|\leq c(1+N_n|A|/V_n)$, uniformly in $n$. Thus $X_n\to P_*(f)$ in probability and the variables are uniformly bounded; for each $\epsilon>0$, $|E X_n-P_*(f)|\leq\epsilon+(M+|P_*(f)|)\Pr(|X_n-P_*(f)|>\epsilon)$ for a common bound $M$, so $E X_n\to P_*(f)$. Torus translation invariance and [F9] identify $E X_n=C_n^{\rm pos}[f]$. Hence the exact-$N_n$ canonical positional local expectations also converge to $P_*$. [A1, F4, F5, F6, F9, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Fix $d\geq1$ and let $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be the numerical even Borel pair potential. Assume the stability, cell-superstability, lower-regularity, and decreasing-integrable-tail conditions of [[def-csm-stable-superstable-continuum-interaction]], with its fixed cell side $\ell$, and the superstable regular interaction, unit-coordinate, and periodic-image conventions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. These are model hypotheses; the definitions do not prove that a particular material satisfies them. Use the finite-region phase-space and statistical-state conventions of [[def-csm-statistical-state-observable]].

Let $E_0>0$ joules be the energy unit, $\ell_0>0$ metres the length unit, $m>0$ kilograms the particle mass, and $p_*>0$ kg m s$^{-1}$ the momentum reference. A physical position vector $\mathbf q_{\rm phys}\in\mathbb R^d$ in metres has dimensionless numerical coordinate $x=\mathbf q_{\rm phys}/\ell_0$. From here on, $q\subseteq\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ denotes a finite configuration of these numerical coordinates, so the physical cube has side $\ell_0L$ and its points are $\ell_0x$. Each momentum mark $p_x\in\mathbb R^d$ is an SI momentum vector in kg m s$^{-1}$. Write $V_L=L^d$ for numerical volume. Fix also a primitive positive scalar conversion parameter $k_B$ with units J K$^{-1}$, called the Boltzmann constant: the thermal-energy scale assigned to temperature $T$ is $k_BT$ joules. Its value is fixed as part of the model data, not derived by this mathematical definition. If $T>0$ kelvin, put $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and $b=\beta_{\rm phys}E_0=E_0/(k_BT)>0$.

The potential $\phi$ in the two interaction suppliers is numerical in units of $E_0$ and takes dimensionless displacements as input. For a physical displacement $\mathbf r\in\mathbb R^d$ measured in metres, its pair-potential map is $V_{\rm pair}(\mathbf r):=E_0\phi(\mathbf r/\ell_0)$ joules. For a finite positional configuration $q\subseteq\Lambda_L$, set $U_{L,\mathrm{free}}(q):=H_\phi(q)$ using [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and set $U_{L,\mathrm{per}}(q):=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(q)$ using that item's periodic-image sum. The periodic definition is used only for periods for which that sum is defined; the large-$L$ results below use sufficiently large periods as supplied there. Thus $E_0U_{L,bc}$ is the dimensional pair energy in either boundary convention.

Let $Q_L$ be the unit-intensity Poisson probability on positional configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, defined by [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Its $N$-particle conditional law $Q_{L,N}$ is uniform on the unordered simple $N$-point configurations; in labelled coordinates it is $L^{-dN}dx_1\cdots dx_N$ on the no-collision set. A finite marked configuration in this sector is a simple set $\xi=\{(x,p_x):x\in q\}$ with $q\subseteq\Lambda_L$, $N(q)=N$, and $p_x\in\mathbb R^d$. Equip the finite marked sector with the sigma-algebra generated by the counts $N_{A\times C}(\xi)=\#\{(x,p_x)\in\xi:x\in A,\ p_x\in C\}$ for bounded Borel $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and Borel $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$. Let $\lambda_d$ be Lebesgue measure on the SI numerical momentum coordinates and set $r:=p_*^{-d}\lambda_d$. For each fixed $q=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}$, define $r^{\otimes q}$ as the image of $r^{\otimes N}$ under $(p_1,\ldots,p_N)\mapsto\{(x_j,p_j):1\le j\le N\}$; this is independent of the enumeration of $q$ because $r^{\otimes N}$ is permutation-invariant. The cell-code representation in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]] supplies a measurable enumeration on each finite sector, so $q\mapsto r^{\otimes q}$ is a measurable kernel for the marked-count sigma-algebra. The finite phase reference is
$$R_{L,N}(dq,dp):=Q_L(dq)\,r^{\otimes q}(dp)\,1_{\{N(q)=N\}}.$$
It is sigma-finite, meaning the marked sector is covered by countably many measurable sets of finite reference measure: for each integer $k\geq1$, restrict to marks satisfying $|p_x|\leq kp_*$ for every one of the $N$ points. These sets exhaust the sector, and their reference measures are at most $Q_L(N(q)=N)r(B_k)^N<\infty$, where $B_k=\{p:|p|\leq kp_*\}$ satisfies $r(B_k)\leq(2k)^d$ because it lies in the box $[-kp_*,kp_*]^d$ of Lebesgue volume $(2kp_*)^d$ by the box-volume supplier in the dependency closure of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. The factor $e^{-V_L}/N!$ from the Poisson sector is retained. In physical coordinates the corresponding one-particle product scale is $h_{\rm ref}^d=\ell_0^dp_*^d$, an action to the power $d$; it is a reference convention, not a derived quantum constant.

For a marked configuration define the total dimensionless energy
$$\mathcal H_{L,bc}(q,p)=U_{L,bc}(q)+\sum_{x\in q}K(p_x),\qquad K(p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2mE_0}.$$
The corresponding physical Hamiltonian is $H^{\rm phys}_{L,bc}:=E_0\mathcal H_{L,bc}$ joules, so $\beta_{\rm phys}H^{\rm phys}_{L,bc}=b\mathcal H_{L,bc}$.
For $b>0$, [[lem-csm-gaussian-mark-moments]] gives $\kappa_b=\int e^{-bK}r(dp)=(2\pi mE_0/(bp_*^2))^{d/2}$ and the probability kernel $\nu_b(dp)=\kappa_b^{-1}e^{-bK(p)}r(dp)$. Whenever the positional canonical partition is finite and positive, nonnegative product integration [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] gives exact identities
$$Z^{\rm ph}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b)=\int e^{-b\mathcal H_{L,bc}}dR_{L,N}=\kappa_b^N Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b),\qquad C^{\rm ph}_{L,N,bc}=C^{\rm pos}_{L,N,bc}\,\nu_b^{\otimes q}.$$
Here $Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}=E_{Q_L}[1_{\{N(q)=N\}}e^{-bU_{L,bc}}]$ and the canonical probabilities are the normalized respective integrands. Under a full grand preparation of activity $z_{\rm ph}$, integrating each momentum changes the positional activity to $z=z_{\rm ph}\kappa_b$; thus a positional activity $z=e^\alpha$ corresponds to $z_{\rm ph}=e^\alpha/\kappa_b$. These are exact definitions and normalizations; they do not assert dynamical equilibration or finite-volume grand convergence. Write $\mathbb T_L^d:=\mathbb R^d/L\mathbb Z^d$ for the periodic position space, represented by $\Lambda_L$; translations act modulo $L$, and the translation-average is Lebesgue measure on $\Lambda_L$ divided by $V_L$. For periodic boundary conditions, simultaneous translation of all positions modulo the period preserves $R_{L,N}$ and $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$: the conditional position law is uniform on $\mathbb T_L^d$, the mark reference is invariant under relabelling points, and the image energy depends only on pair displacements. Hence normalized canonical and finite band restrictions are invariant under every such translation.

Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC and HB, the exact superstable regular pair interaction and periodic-image convention of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], and integer side lengths $L_n\to\infty$ with exact particle numbers $N_n/V_n\to\rho>0$ at an interior attainable density. Fix $b>0$. Assume the positional canonical log rate is $F_b(\rho)$, and choose finite $\alpha$ with
$$P_{\rm Leb}(α,b)=F_b(ρ)+αρ,$$
where $P_{\rm Leb}$ is the grand pressure per numerical volume with Lebesgue $1/N!$ normalization. Let the positional grand variational minimizer of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]] at activity $\exp(\alpha)$ and inverse temperature $b$ be the singleton $\{P_*\}$. Let $R_n=R_{L_n,N_n}$ be the phase reference of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], let $A_n$ be the band of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]], set $M_n^{\rm ph}(E)=R_n(E\cap A_n)/R_n(A_n)$, and let $B_n$ be its positional marginal. For any local-tame test $f$, write $B_n[f]=E_{B_n}f(\omega^{(L_n)})$ and $C_n^{\rm pos}[f]=E_{C_n^{\rm pos}}f(\omega^{(L_n)})$, where $\omega^{(L_n)}$ is the periodic continuation. Let $\bar B_n$ be the barycenter of $R_{L_n,\omega}$ under $B_n$. Then $\bar B_n$ converges to $P_*$ in $\tau_L$, equivalently $B_n[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every local-tame $f$; also $C_n^{\rm pos}[f]\to P_*(f)$ for every such $f$. Here $P_*$ is an infinite-volume positional variational state; no finite-volume grand-canonical local convergence or DLR identification is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$. For $i\in\mathbb Z^d$, let $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$. These are left-closed, right-open cells. For every $x\in\mathbb R^d$, [[lem-integer-part]] supplies the unique integers $i_j$ with $i_j\le x_j<i_j+1$, so $x$ belongs to exactly one $C_i$. The cells are Borel products of closed/open ray intersections and have volume one by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], whose statement covers this face convention. A finite configuration in $C_i$ is a finite subset of distinct points. Encode it by its cardinality $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and its uniquely lexicographically increasing list of local coordinates $(x_1-i,\ldots,x_n-i)\in([0,1)^d)^n$. Pad the code after its first $n$ coordinates with the zero vector. For fixed $n$, the strictly increasing lists form a Borel subset of $([0,1]^d)^n$, since lexicographic strict order is a finite union of coordinate-equality and coordinate-inequality conditions. Thus all codes form a Borel subset of $\mathbb N_0\times([0,1]^d)^{\mathbb N}$. Each factor $[0,1]^d$ is Polish as a closed subspace of complete $\mathbb R^d$ with a countable dense rational grid; $\mathbb N_0$ with its discrete metric is Polish. The ambient space is Polish by [[cor-countable-products-and-g-delta-subspaces-of-polish-spaces-are-polish]] (and is completely metrized by [[lem-standard-complete-metric-on-a-countable-product]]), so [[lem-borel-subspaces-admit-polish-presentations]] makes the cell space $E_i$ standard Borel. By [[lem-tdmath-counts-generate-configuration-sigma]], its sigma-algebra is generated by the counts $N_B$ for Borel $B\subseteq C_i$.

Use $e^t:=\exp(t)$ for real $t$, with $\exp$ defined by [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]; for a real measurable function $f$, $e^f$ means the pointwise composition $\exp\circ f$. For $\lambda>0$, give a cell configuration with $n$ points probability $\exp(-\lambda)\lambda^n/n!$ for its count. The probabilities sum to $\exp(-\lambda)\exp(\lambda)=\exp(0)=1$ by the exponential power series and [[thm-exponential-addition-formula]]. Conditional on count $n$, take the $n$-fold product of normalized Lebesgue measure on $C_i$, restrict it to the complement of the collision diagonals, and push it forward by lexicographic sorting. The product exists by the finite product-measure theorem; each collision diagonal is null by Tonelli and the fact that Lebesgue measure gives every singleton measure zero, so the restricted measure still has mass one. Sorting is Borel on the finitely many permutation regions of the no-collision set. This defines a law $\pi_{i,\lambda}$ on $E_i$; for $n=0$, use the empty product and the empty configuration. Let $\Omega=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}E_i$ with its product cylinder sigma-algebra. The product sigma-algebra is generated by the cell-coordinate sigma-algebras, each generated by counts on Borel subsets of its bounded cell by [[lem-tdmath-counts-generate-configuration-sigma]]. Conversely every bounded-region count is a finite sum of these cell counts, since a bounded set meets finitely many cells. Thus the product cylinder sigma-algebra is exactly the sigma-algebra generated by all bounded-Borel count maps. For each $\lambda>0$, $Q_\lambda$ denotes the unique probability on $\Omega$ whose finite cell marginals are the products of the corresponding $\pi_{i,\lambda}$. Existence and uniqueness follow from [[thm-kolmogorov-extension-for-standard-borel-coordinate-spaces]]. In particular every translation $T_x$ is measurable since $N_A(T_x\omega)=N_{A-x}(\omega)$. The unit-intensity reference is $Q:=Q_1$.

Identify each $\omega\in\Omega$ with the simple locally finite counting measure obtained by uniting its finite cell configurations. For a bounded Borel set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, write $N_A(\omega)=\omega(A)$ and $|A|$ for its Lebesgue measure. Define translation by $T_x\omega(A)=\omega(A-x)$ for $x\in\mathbb R^d$. The next item proves that under $Q_\lambda$, counts in disjoint bounded Borel sets are independent Poisson random variables with means $\lambda|A|$ and that $Q_\lambda$ is translation invariant. This item is a mathematical reference construction and makes no physical claim.

Let $\Omega$ be the positional configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. The **marked configuration space** $\Omega^{\rm mark}$ consists of marked point sets $\xi\subseteq\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d$ with spatial projection $q=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\exists p\in\mathbb R^d,\ (x,p)\in\xi\}$ that is simple and locally finite, and with exactly one mark $p_x$ paired to each $x\in q$. Its sigma-algebra is generated by the marked counts $N_{A\times C}(\xi)=\#\{(x,p)\in\xi:x\in A,\ p\in C\}$ for bounded Borel $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and Borel $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$. The positional projection is $\pi(\xi)=q\in\Omega$. For a bounded Borel set $\Delta$, the **marked local restriction** is $\xi_\Delta=\{(x,p)\in\xi:x\in\Delta\}$ with the induced count sigma-algebra; write $N_\Delta(\xi)=\#\xi_\Delta$. A **marked-local observable on $\Delta$** is a real measurable function of $\xi_\Delta$; it is bounded when its supremum norm is finite.

Let $d\geq1$, $L>0$, and $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$. A finite marked configuration consists of a finite simple set of positions $q\subseteq\Lambda_L$ and a mark map $p:q\to\mathbb R^d$, as in [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]. Its **marked periodic continuation** is
$$\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}:=\{(x+Lk,p_x):x\in q,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}.$$
The spatial positions in this set are distinct: if $x+Lk=y+Lj$ for $x,y\in[0,L)^d$, then coordinatewise $x-y=L(j-k)$ forces $j=k$ and $x=y$. Every bounded spatial region meets finitely many lattice translates of the finite set $q$, so the continuation has a locally finite spatial projection.

For a bounded Borel set $\Delta\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, define its **marked local restriction** by
$$\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}|_\Delta:=\{(y,p_x)\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}_{L,q,p}:y\in\Delta\}.$$
This is an element of $\Omega^{\rm mark}$, with the induced sigma-algebra of marked counts above. If $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda_L$, the restriction is exactly the original marked points with positions in $\Delta$.

Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be standard-Borel spaces, let $Q_i$ be probability measures on $X_i$, and let $P$ be a probability on $\prod_{i=1}^mX_i$. Write $P_i$ for its $i$th marginal and use the directional extended relative entropy $D(\cdot\Vert\cdot)$ of [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q_1\otimes\cdots\otimes Q_m)\geq\sum_{i=1}^mD(P_i\Vert Q_i).$$
If the left side is finite, the conditional chain rule gives the stronger equality
$$D(P\Vert\textstyle\bigotimes_iQ_i)=D(P_1\Vert Q_1)+\sum_{i=2}^m E_P\,D(P_{X_i\mid X_1,\ldots,X_{i-1}}\Vert Q_i),$$
and each conditional increment is at least $D(P_i\Vert Q_i)$. If the left side is infinite, the displayed inequality is understood in the extended order and is automatic. For an integer $d\ge1$ and disjoint spatial blocks with fixed particle counts $n_i\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and fixed positions, apply this result to their mark spaces $X_i=(\mathbb R^d)^{n_i}$, with Borel sigma-algebras and probability mark references $Q_i$. The zero-fold product $X_i=(\mathbb R^d)^0$ is the singleton consisting of the empty mark tuple. On that singleton both $P_i$ and $Q_i$ are its unique probability measure, so a zero-occupancy mark block contributes zero. No zero-divergence claim is made for an unconditioned occupancy law.

Assume AC. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on a measurable space and let $T$ be a measurable map to another measurable space. Then
$$D(T_*P\Vert T_*Q)\leq D(P\Vert Q),\qquad \|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}:=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|\leq\sqrt{D(P\Vert Q)/2}.$$
The entropy convention is the directional KL definition of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]], and the total-variation convention is the event-supremum convention of [[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]]. The inequality remains valid when $D=+\infty$.

Assume AC and the hypotheses and notation of [[thm-csm-total-canonical-window]]. Let $R_n=R_{L_n,N_n}$ be the finite phase reference of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], let $A_n$ be the constructed band, and set $M_n^{\rm ph}(E)=R_n(E\cap A_n)/R_n(A_n)$. Let $C_n^{\rm ph}$ be the full fixed-$N_n$ canonical probability. Then $D_n=D(M_n^{\rm ph}\Vert C_n^{\rm ph})$ satisfies $D_n/V_n\to0$. This is a mathematical statement about a normalized measure restriction; it does not assert $D_n\to0$ or global total-variation convergence.

derivations.claim:
The phase reference has a measurable density. For each $q$, integrate the band indicator over the $N_n$-mark reference; Tonelli gives a measurable normalizer. On the $B_n$-full set where it is positive, division gives the conditional kernel $b_n(\cdot|q)$; choose a fixed probability kernel on the null complement. The conditional chain rule, nonnegativity of the positional divergence, and [F3] give
$$J_n:=E_{B_n}D(b_n(.|q)||ν_b^{⊗N_n})\le D(M_n^{ph}||C_n^{ph}).$$

For each $q$, partition its finitely many points into those in each of the $L_n^{\rm pack}$ disjoint translates $C_j$ packed in the periodic cube, plus the remainder. This is a measurable finite partition; ordering the points by the cell codes in [F2] identifies each block with a finite-dimensional standard-Borel mark space, even though its size depends on $q$. The Gaussian product reference factors over these disjoint sets. Applying [F3] conditionally gives
$$D(b_n(.|q)||ν_b^{⊗N_n})\ge\sum_{j=1}^{L_n^{pack}}D(b_{n,j}(.|q)||ν_b^{⊗N_{Δ_j}(q)}),$$
where an empty block contributes zero. Joint torus-translation invariance transports each block law and its reference kernel, so the integrated divergence is the same for every translate. Averaging and discarding the nonnegative remainder term bounds the divergence for a chosen translate of $C$ by $J_n/L_n^{\rm pack}$.

For $\Delta\subseteq C$, restriction of the ordered mark vector on $q\cap C$ to the points in $q\cap\Delta$ is measurable. Data processing [F4] gives $D(b_{n,\Delta}(\cdot|q)||\nu_b^{\otimes N_\Delta(q)})\leq D(b_{n,C}(\cdot|q)||\nu_b^{\otimes N_C(q)})$ for $B_n$-almost every $q$. Integrating and applying step 2.1 bounds the left side by $J_n/L_n^{\rm pack}$. By [F5], $J_n=o(V_n)$, while $L_n^{\rm pack}/V_n\to1/|C|>0$; therefore the bound tends to zero.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

For standard-Borel spaces $X,Y$, probability reference measures $Q_X,Q_Y$, and a joint probability $P_{XY}\ll Q_X\otimes Q_Y$ with finite $D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)$, let $P_{Y|X=x}$ be the conditional law supplied by [[thm-conditional-density-formula]]. Then
$$D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)=D(P_X\Vert Q_X)+\int_X D(P_{Y|X=x}\Vert Q_Y)\,P_X(dx).$$

$$G(R):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|R}\Vert Q_Y)\right],\qquad G(S):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|S}\Vert Q_Y)\right]$$

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **ultrafilter extension principle** says that every filter on a set is contained in an ultrafilter on that set ([[def-ultrafilter]]).

It is also called the **ultrafilter lemma** and is equivalent over ZF to the Boolean prime ideal theorem, abbreviated BPI. Items below write **assume UL/BPI** precisely when they use this extension principle; they do not thereby assume the full axiom of choice.

Let $X$ be a set and let $R \subseteq X \times X$ be a binary relation on $X$.
Call $R$ **entire on $X$** when

$$\text{for every } x \in X \text{ there is } y \in X \text{ with } x \mathbin{R} y .$$

The **Axiom of Dependent Choice**, written $\mathrm{DC}$, is the following
statement.

> For every nonempty set $X$, every relation $R$ entire on $X$, and every
> $a \in X$, there is a function $x : \mathbb{N} \to X$ ([[def-function]],
> [[def-natural-numbers]]) with
> $$x_0 = a \qquad \text{and} \qquad x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1} \ \text{ for every } n \in \mathbb{N}.$$

Here a sequence in $X$ means a function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $X$, not necessarily
a real-valued sequence. As everywhere in this library $\mathbb{N}$ contains $0$, and the sequence is
indexed from $0$; the term $x_0$ is the prescribed starting point $a$ and every
later term is related to its predecessor.

**What DC adds to what came before.** [[def-choice-function]] and
[[def-axiom-of-choice]] select one element from each member of a family that is
fixed in advance, and [[def-countable-choice]] does the same for a family indexed
by $\mathbb{N}$. In both, the family is given before any selection is made. DC is
the principle needed when the $n$-th set to select from is not known until the
first $n$ selections have been made: here the admissible values of $x_{n+1}$ are
exactly the $R$-successors of $x_n$, so the family being chosen from is built
along the choosing. Thus the displayed recursion is directly an instance of
DC; it is not itself an application of the fixed-family formulation of
countable choice. This observation concerns the input to the two axioms and
makes no claim about a nonimplication between them.

**The starting point may be dropped.** The formally weaker statement obtained by
deleting the clause $x_0 = a$ — for every nonempty $X$ and every entire $R$ there
is a sequence with $x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ for all $n$ — is an immediate
consequence of the form above, since $X$ is nonempty and any of its elements may
be taken as $a$. Conversely, assume the start-free form, and fix $X$, $R$ and $a$ as above. Let $P$ be the set of all functions $p:k\to X$ with nonzero $k\in\mathbb N$, $p(0)=a$, and $p(i)\mathbin R p(i+1)$ whenever $i+1<k$. It is a set by Separation inside $\mathcal P(\mathbb N\times X)$ ([[def-power-set]], [[def-cartesian-product]], [[def-axiom-schema-of-separation]]); a natural is the set of its predecessors ([[lem-nat-order-is-membership]]). The singleton path $\{(0,a)\}$ lies in $P$.

On $P$ let $p\mathbin S q$ mean that $q$ extends $p$ by exactly one new last entry. This relation is entire: for one particular $p:k\to X$, write $k=j+1$ ([[lem-nat-nonzero-is-successor]]); an $R$-successor $y$ of $p(j)$ exists, and $q=p\cup\{(k,y)\}$ is the required extension. This is existential instantiation for that path, not a simultaneous choice of successors. Start-free DC now supplies a sequence $(p_n)$ with $p_n\mathbin S p_{n+1}$; its first path need not be the singleton path, but every path in $P$ already starts at $a$.

Their graphs are nested. By induction ([[thm-induction-principle]]), $p_n$ has at least $n+1$ entries: the initial path is nonempty, and every step adds one entry. Hence $x=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}p_n$ is a function with domain $\mathbb N$ and values in $X$. Indeed, nestedness makes all common values agree, every natural index eventually lies in a path, and no path has indices outside $\mathbb N$. Each path starts at $a$, so $x(0)=a$; for any $i$, a sufficiently long path contains both $i$ and $i+1$, giving $x(i)\mathbin R x(i+1)$. Replacement and Union form this union of the sequence of graphs. Thus the start-free and prescribed-start forms are equivalent in ZF. Every use below retains the prescribed-start convention.

**$R$ need not be an order and the terms need not be distinct.** What DC delivers
is a sequence, that is a function $\mathbb{N} \to X$, not a chain in the
order-theoretic sense ([[def-chain]]). The relation may be symmetric, and the
sequence may repeat a value or be constant; all that is asserted is
$x_n \mathbin{R} x_{n+1}$ at every index.

Work over ZF. The **real dominated-extension principle**, denoted **HB**, is the following assertion:

For every real vector space $X$, every sublinear functional $p:X\to\mathbb R$ in the sense of [[def-sublinear-functional]], every real linear subspace $M\le X$ in the sense of [[def-linear-subspace]], and every real linear functional $g:M\to\mathbb R$ in the sense of [[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]],
$$\bigl(\forall m\in M,\ g(m)\le p(m)\bigr)\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists F:X\to\mathbb R\ \bigl(F\text{ is real linear},\ F|_M=g,\ \forall x\in X,\ F(x)\le p(x)\bigr).$$

This names an additional principle; it does not assert a proof of HB in ZF. Subsequent results explicitly state when they assume HB. Neither topology nor completeness is part of this assertion. The subspace may be $\{0\}$ or all of $X$. Sublinearity at scalar zero gives $p(0)=0$, and a linear functional has value zero at zero.

Assume AC and the hypotheses and notation of [[thm-csm-full-shell-positional-minimizer]], including its AC, ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB assumptions. Fix a bounded Borel region $\Delta$ and use the marked periodic continuation and local restriction defined in [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]]. By translating $\Delta$ and the spatial argument of $G$ together, take a representative with $\Delta\subseteq[0,\infty)^d$; then $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda_{L_n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. This translation preserves the expectations because the finite laws are torus-translation invariant and the limiting independent mark lift of the stationary positional state is stationary. Let $M_n^{\rm ph}$ be the uniform full-phase band law, $C_n^{\rm ph}$ the exact-$N_n$ full canonical law, and $P_*$ the singleton positional grand variational minimizer. Give points of $P_*$ independent marks with kernel $\nu_b$ of [[def-csm-full-marked-model]], and denote the resulting infinite marked law by $P_*^{\rm mark}$, whose existence is supplied by [[lem-csm-gaussian-marked-lift-existence]]. For finite-volume expectations, evaluate $G$ on the restriction $\omega^{\rm per}_{L_n,q,p}|_\Delta$; under $P_*^{\rm mark}$, evaluate it on $\xi_\Delta$. Then for every bounded marked-local observable $G$ on $\Delta$ in the sense of [[def-csm-marked-periodic-continuation]],
$$E_{M_n^{ph}}G\to E_{P_*^{mark}}G,\qquad E_{C_n^{ph}}G\to E_{P_*^{mark}}G.$$
The matched full grand activity is $\exp(\alpha)/\kappa_b$ by the normalization identity in [[def-csm-full-marked-model]]; $P_*^{\rm mark}$ is the independent-Gaussian marked lift associated with that positional variational minimizer. If additionally $|G|\leq C(1+N_\Delta)$, shell convergence also holds for $G$. This is fixed-region convergence, not uniform over growing regions or arbitrary unbounded momentum observables. No finite-volume grand-canonical convergence or DLR converse is asserted.

Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[thm-csm-local-mark-kl-bound]]. Fix a bounded half-open cube $\Delta\subseteq[0,\infty)^d$; then $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda_{L_n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. By torus translation invariance this placement gives the same limits as any fixed translate of the cube. Let $N_\Delta(q)=\#(q\cap\Delta)$. For $b>0$ and $K(p)=|p|^2/(2mE_0)$, the full shell law satisfies
$$E_{M_n^{ph}}\sum_{x\in q\cap\Delta}K(p_x)\to dρ|Δ|/(2b),\quad E_{M_n^{ph}}\sum_{x\in q\cap\Delta}p_{x,i}\to0,$$
$$E_{M_n^{ph}}\sum_{x\in q\cap\Delta}p_{x,i}p_{x,j}\to(mE_0ρ|Δ|/b)\delta_{ij}.$$
The corresponding canonical and marked variational-grand laws have the same limits by their independent Gaussian marking. Momentum is in kg m s^-1, E_0K is in joules, and b=E_0/(k_BT) is dimensionless. These conclusions concern only the named moments, not every unbounded mark observable.

Assume AC. Fix $d\geq1$ and let $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ be the numerical even Borel pair potential. Assume the stability, cell-superstability, lower-regularity, and decreasing-integrable-tail conditions of [[def-csm-stable-superstable-continuum-interaction]], with its fixed cell side $\ell$, and the superstable regular interaction, unit-coordinate, and periodic-image conventions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. These are model hypotheses; the definitions do not prove that a particular material satisfies them. Use the finite-region phase-space and statistical-state conventions of [[def-csm-statistical-state-observable]].

Let $E_0>0$ joules be the energy unit, $\ell_0>0$ metres the length unit, $m>0$ kilograms the particle mass, and $p_*>0$ kg m s$^{-1}$ the momentum reference. A physical position vector $\mathbf q_{\rm phys}\in\mathbb R^d$ in metres has dimensionless numerical coordinate $x=\mathbf q_{\rm phys}/\ell_0$. From here on, $q\subseteq\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ denotes a finite configuration of these numerical coordinates, so the physical cube has side $\ell_0L$ and its points are $\ell_0x$. Each momentum mark $p_x\in\mathbb R^d$ is an SI momentum vector in kg m s$^{-1}$. Write $V_L=L^d$ for numerical volume. Fix also a primitive positive scalar conversion parameter $k_B$ with units J K$^{-1}$, called the Boltzmann constant: the thermal-energy scale assigned to temperature $T$ is $k_BT$ joules. Its value is fixed as part of the model data, not derived by this mathematical definition. If $T>0$ kelvin, put $\beta_{\rm phys}=1/(k_BT)$ in J$^{-1}$ and $b=\beta_{\rm phys}E_0=E_0/(k_BT)>0$.

The potential $\phi$ in the two interaction suppliers is numerical in units of $E_0$ and takes dimensionless displacements as input. For a physical displacement $\mathbf r\in\mathbb R^d$ measured in metres, its pair-potential map is $V_{\rm pair}(\mathbf r):=E_0\phi(\mathbf r/\ell_0)$ joules. For a finite positional configuration $q\subseteq\Lambda_L$, set $U_{L,\mathrm{free}}(q):=H_\phi(q)$ using [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and set $U_{L,\mathrm{per}}(q):=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(q)$ using that item's periodic-image sum. The periodic definition is used only for periods for which that sum is defined; the large-$L$ results below use sufficiently large periods as supplied there. Thus $E_0U_{L,bc}$ is the dimensional pair energy in either boundary convention.

Let $Q_L$ be the unit-intensity Poisson probability on positional configurations in $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, defined by [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Its $N$-particle conditional law $Q_{L,N}$ is uniform on the unordered simple $N$-point configurations; in labelled coordinates it is $L^{-dN}dx_1\cdots dx_N$ on the no-collision set. A finite marked configuration in this sector is a simple set $\xi=\{(x,p_x):x\in q\}$ with $q\subseteq\Lambda_L$, $N(q)=N$, and $p_x\in\mathbb R^d$. Equip the finite marked sector with the sigma-algebra generated by the counts $N_{A\times C}(\xi)=\#\{(x,p_x)\in\xi:x\in A,\ p_x\in C\}$ for bounded Borel $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and Borel $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$. Let $\lambda_d$ be Lebesgue measure on the SI numerical momentum coordinates and set $r:=p_*^{-d}\lambda_d$. For each fixed $q=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}$, define $r^{\otimes q}$ as the image of $r^{\otimes N}$ under $(p_1,\ldots,p_N)\mapsto\{(x_j,p_j):1\le j\le N\}$; this is independent of the enumeration of $q$ because $r^{\otimes N}$ is permutation-invariant. The cell-code representation in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]] supplies a measurable enumeration on each finite sector, so $q\mapsto r^{\otimes q}$ is a measurable kernel for the marked-count sigma-algebra. The finite phase reference is
$$R_{L,N}(dq,dp):=Q_L(dq)\,r^{\otimes q}(dp)\,1_{\{N(q)=N\}}.$$
It is sigma-finite, meaning the marked sector is covered by countably many measurable sets of finite reference measure: for each integer $k\geq1$, restrict to marks satisfying $|p_x|\leq kp_*$ for every one of the $N$ points. These sets exhaust the sector, and their reference measures are at most $Q_L(N(q)=N)r(B_k)^N<\infty$, where $B_k=\{p:|p|\leq kp_*\}$ satisfies $r(B_k)\leq(2k)^d$ because it lies in the box $[-kp_*,kp_*]^d$ of Lebesgue volume $(2kp_*)^d$ by the box-volume supplier in the dependency closure of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. The factor $e^{-V_L}/N!$ from the Poisson sector is retained. In physical coordinates the corresponding one-particle product scale is $h_{\rm ref}^d=\ell_0^dp_*^d$, an action to the power $d$; it is a reference convention, not a derived quantum constant.

For a marked configuration define the total dimensionless energy
$$\mathcal H_{L,bc}(q,p)=U_{L,bc}(q)+\sum_{x\in q}K(p_x),\qquad K(p)=\frac{|p|^2}{2mE_0}.$$
The corresponding physical Hamiltonian is $H^{\rm phys}_{L,bc}:=E_0\mathcal H_{L,bc}$ joules, so $\beta_{\rm phys}H^{\rm phys}_{L,bc}=b\mathcal H_{L,bc}$.
For $b>0$, [[lem-csm-gaussian-mark-moments]] gives $\kappa_b=\int e^{-bK}r(dp)=(2\pi mE_0/(bp_*^2))^{d/2}$ and the probability kernel $\nu_b(dp)=\kappa_b^{-1}e^{-bK(p)}r(dp)$. Whenever the positional canonical partition is finite and positive, nonnegative product integration [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] gives exact identities
$$Z^{\rm ph}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b)=\int e^{-b\mathcal H_{L,bc}}dR_{L,N}=\kappa_b^N Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}(b),\qquad C^{\rm ph}_{L,N,bc}=C^{\rm pos}_{L,N,bc}\,\nu_b^{\otimes q}.$$
Here $Z^{\rm pos}_{Q,L,N,bc}=E_{Q_L}[1_{\{N(q)=N\}}e^{-bU_{L,bc}}]$ and the canonical probabilities are the normalized respective integrands. Under a full grand preparation of activity $z_{\rm ph}$, integrating each momentum changes the positional activity to $z=z_{\rm ph}\kappa_b$; thus a positional activity $z=e^\alpha$ corresponds to $z_{\rm ph}=e^\alpha/\kappa_b$. These are exact definitions and normalizations; they do not assert dynamical equilibration or finite-volume grand convergence. Write $\mathbb T_L^d:=\mathbb R^d/L\mathbb Z^d$ for the periodic position space, represented by $\Lambda_L$; translations act modulo $L$, and the translation-average is Lebesgue measure on $\Lambda_L$ divided by $V_L$. For periodic boundary conditions, simultaneous translation of all positions modulo the period preserves $R_{L,N}$ and $\mathcal H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$: the conditional position law is uniform on $\mathbb T_L^d$, the mark reference is invariant under relabelling points, and the image energy depends only on pair displacements. Hence normalized canonical and finite band restrictions are invariant under every such translation.

derivations.claim: A fixed bounded marked-local observable is bounded on its named region, so [F1] applies directly to shell and canonical preparations. Their common limiting law is the independent Gaussian mark lift of the positional grand variational minimizer $P_*$. citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be standard-Borel spaces, let $Q_i$ be probability measures on $X_i$, and let $P$ be a probability on $\prod_{i=1}^mX_i$. Write $P_i$ for its $i$th marginal and use the directional extended relative entropy $D(\cdot\Vert\cdot)$ of [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q_1\otimes\cdots\otimes Q_m)\geq\sum_{i=1}^mD(P_i\Vert Q_i).$$
If the left side is finite, the conditional chain rule gives the stronger equality
$$D(P\Vert\textstyle\bigotimes_iQ_i)=D(P_1\Vert Q_1)+\sum_{i=2}^m E_P\,D(P_{X_i\mid X_1,\ldots,X_{i-1}}\Vert Q_i),$$
and each conditional increment is at least $D(P_i\Vert Q_i)$. If the left side is infinite, the displayed inequality is understood in the extended order and is automatic. For an integer $d\ge1$ and disjoint spatial blocks with fixed particle counts $n_i\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and fixed positions, apply this result to their mark spaces $X_i=(\mathbb R^d)^{n_i}$, with Borel sigma-algebras and probability mark references $Q_i$. The zero-fold product $X_i=(\mathbb R^d)^0$ is the singleton consisting of the empty mark tuple. On that singleton both $P_i$ and $Q_i$ are its unique probability measure, so a zero-occupancy mark block contributes zero. No zero-divergence claim is made for an unconditioned occupancy law.

derivations.claim: Set $A_N:=\delta_1\otimes\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\theta)^{\otimes(N-1)}$, using the empty product for $N=1$. Under $A_N$, $X_1=1$ surely and the remaining coordinates retain their independent Bernoulli-$\theta$ law. The likelihood $dA_N/dP_N$ is $1/\theta$ on $\{X_1=1\}$ and zero elsewhere, so integration gives $D(A_N\Vert P_N)=\log(1/\theta)$. Equivalently, [F1] decomposes the divergence into $D(\delta_1\Vert\mathrm{Bernoulli}(\theta))=\log(1/\theta)$ and a zero conditional remainder. Dividing by $N$ gives vanishing entropy density.

Under $A_N$, $H_N=\epsilon(1+Y_N)$ with $Y_N$ binomial $(N-1,\theta)$. Since $Y_N$ is the sum of $N-1$ independent Bernoulli coordinates, $E Y_N=(N-1)\theta$ and $\operatorname{Var}(Y_N)=(N-1)\theta(1-\theta)$, by expanding the mean and variance and using zero cross-covariances. Thus $E(H_N/N)=\epsilon[1+(N-1)\theta]/N\to\epsilon\theta$ and $\operatorname{Var}(H_N/N)=\epsilon^2(N-1)\theta(1-\theta)/N^2\to0$. For any $\eta>0$, $1_{\{|H_N/N-E(H_N/N)|\geq\eta\}}\leq(H_N/N-E(H_N/N))^2/\eta^2$; integrating gives the Chebyshev bound and convergence in probability. Its Shannon entropy is $H_{\rm Sh}(A_N)=(N-1)h(\theta)$ by adding the logarithms of the independent-coordinate probabilities, so $H_{\rm Sh}(A_N)/N=(N-1)h(\theta)/N\to h(\theta)$, where $h(\theta)=-\theta\log\theta-(1-\theta)\log(1-\theta)$. Yet the first coordinate remains one and is at total-variation distance $1-\theta$ from Bernoulli$(\theta)$. This proves all claims and refutes the statement. [step 1.1, algebra] ∎
